beastkin.adaptations: Enhanced chemical and thermal senses; moisture-absorbing palms, soles, and sensory nodes around the throat and neck.
beastkin.appearance: Wolf-like features, dense muscle and bone, and semi-retractable claws.
beastkin.combat_role: Close-quarters vanguards with strong stagger potential and terrain traversal.
beastkin.culture: Pack-oriented communities with strong bonds and clan identity.
beastkin.habitat: Varied; often organized around pack and clan communities.
beastkin.name: Beastkin
beastkin.notes: The bible distinguishes Beastkin from were-creatures, which it describes as the result of later experiments.

fairies_nymphs.culture: Known as fae in western traditions and Tianling in eastern traditions.
fairies_nymphs.name: Fairies / Nymphs
fairies_nymphs.notes: A broad category in the source taxonomy; individual kinds and cultures remain open for authoring.

featherfolk.adaptations: Gliding and flight-oriented bodies; wing joints and lower legs absorb atmospheric moisture.
featherfolk.appearance: Feathered, winged humanoids with reinforced lightweight bones.
featherfolk.combat_role: Aerial mobility, glide-dodges, and wind-based maneuvering.
featherfolk.culture: Communities value aerial travel, weather knowledge, and wind-weaving traditions.
featherfolk.habitat: Highlands, cliffs, and regions with reliable updrafts and aetheric winds.
featherfolk.name: Featherfolk
featherfolk.naming: Light consonants and wind- or sky-inspired phonetics.
featherfolk.notes: The source bible describes reverse sexual size dimorphism; this can be refined as character designs are developed.

gharuk.adaptations: Heat-venting dermal ridges and moisture-absorbing palms and soles adapted to dry soils. Water scarcity is a serious environmental challenge.
gharuk.appearance: Compact, blocky build with dense muscle; olive-green to moss-bronze skin and coarse, dark hair.
gharuk.combat_role: Compact, powerful fighters; forge and scouting traditions influence their combat styles.
gharuk.culture: Clan and Forge-Hold communities. Oral epics, forge markings, mentorship, and the ideal 'Burn bright, pass the flame' are central.
gharuk.habitat: Arid regions, forge-holds, clay basins, and moisture-retaining deserts.
gharuk.maturation: Rapid; commonly considered adult between 8 and 12 years.
gharuk.name: Gharuk
gharuk.naming: Panslavonic and Proto-Indo-European roots, with Solani nautical loanwords.
gharuk.notes: Use water access and climate as meaningful setting factors without treating any Gharuk individual as defined solely by them.

kaeli.adaptations: Lower innate mana affinity than many peoples, balanced by stamina, chemical efficiency, and adaptability.
kaeli.appearance: Broadly varied; adaptable across climates and communities.
kaeli.combat_role: Adaptable generalists; individual skills and regional training vary widely.
kaeli.culture: Highly diverse. Trade and contact with other peoples have shaped many human societies.
kaeli.habitat: Wide-ranging; human cultures span kingdoms, republics, and cultivation clans.
kaeli.lifespan: 120–150 years in a mana- and leyline-rich world.
kaeli.name: Kaeli
kaeli.naming: Panslavonic, Interslavic, and Proto-Indo-European roots, with Latin loanwords from Solani trade.
kaeli.notes: Kaeli are the human people and serve as a cultural and biological bridge among several peoples.

sirens_mermaids.culture: The source bible groups these among Jin, with regional interpretations.
sirens_mermaids.name: Sirens / Mermaids
sirens_mermaids.notes: Further distinctions between sirens and mermaids are left editable.

solani.adaptations: Adapted to direct sun and salt air. Moisture-absorbing tissues filter salt; resin-like skin layers help limit water loss.
solani.appearance: Stockier and more muscular than the Sylvani, with bronze or tanned skin; leaf-like ears and root-like hair.
solani.combat_role: Durable coastal and desert travelers, with strong trade and maritime traditions.
solani.culture: Outgoing, mercantile, and seafaring. Clan councils govern communities; salt trade and Brine-Master routes are culturally important.
solani.habitat: Desert, tropical, and coastal regions; prominent seafaring communities.
solani.maturation: Similar long maturation to the Sylvani.
solani.name: Solani
solani.naming: Latin-influenced names with regional phonetic shifts.
solani.notes: The Solani share elven ancestry with the Sylvani but have distinct regional adaptations and social traditions.

elementals.adaptations: Sustained by leyline flow; their expression reflects elemental affinity.
elementals.appearance: Form and dominant coloration reflect elemental affinity.
elementals.habitat: Leyline-rich regions and places associated with their elemental affinity.
elementals.name: Elementals

spirits.adaptations: Sustained by leyline flow; their expression reflects elemental affinity.
spirits.appearance: Form and dominant coloration reflect elemental affinity.
spirits.habitat: Leyline-rich regions and places associated with their elemental affinity.
spirits.name: Spirits

sylvani.adaptations: Root-like hair structure; supplemental photosynthesis; palms and soles absorb moisture from moss, bark, leaf litter, and dew.
sylvani.appearance: Tall, lean build; pale to pinkish skin; leaf-like ears. Silver or blonde hair is common; crimson is rare, and grey or white is associated with strong mana affinity.
sylvani.combat_role: Patient, resilient combatants with strong affinity for sustained mana use.
sylvani.culture: Historically isolationist, with traditions of patience, lineage, and leyline meditation. Governance shifted from matriarchal monarchy to a representative conclave.
sylvani.maturation: Slow maturation; full maturity around 30 years.
sylvani.name: Sylvani
sylvani.naming: Old Norse and Germanic roots with Latin scholarly influence.
sylvani.notes: The Sylvani are the temperate elven people. Individual traits and regional traditions may vary.

treesprites_dryads.culture: Sylvani traditions call them Andvari and regard them as nature's breath.
treesprites_dryads.habitat: Woodlands and places of strong natural resonance.
treesprites_dryads.name: Treesprites / Dryads
treesprites_dryads.notes: The source bible groups these among woodland fae.

undead.culture: Feared and studied; some may be bargained with.
undead.name: Undead
undead.notes: The source bible describes chaotic-evil alignment as common, not universal.

vampires.adaptations: Described in the source bible as the result of Dark Age human experiments.
vampires.culture: Often regarded as cursed nobility; some practice blood magic.
vampires.name: Vampires
vampires.notes: Their origin is not widely known in the modern era.

veylkai.adaptations: Powerful mana affinity; their presence influences mana tides and regional seasons.
veylkai.combat_role: Deity-tier beings; alignment and local relationship affect their role in a region.
veylkai.culture: Communicate through harmonic frequencies known as the Chorus. They do not self-title; mortals give them local names.
veylkai.habitat: Regionally varied; strongly connected to planetary mana.
veylkai.name: Dragons (Veyl'kai)
veylkai.naming: Region-specific names given by local peoples.
veylkai.notes: The source bible describes dragons as planetary mana magnets.

were_creatures.culture: Described in the source bible as a Dark Age human experiment, called 'Strain β'.
were_creatures.name: Were-Creatures
were_creatures.notes: The source bible distinguishes these from naturally occurring Beastkin.
